items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally increase down a group?

rubric.why: Elements farther down a group have more occupied electron shells.
rubric.description: States that an additional electron shell is present down the group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in electron shells.

accept: inner shell electrons shield the outer electrons
rubric.why: The extra inner-shell electrons shield the outer electrons from the nucleus.
rubric.description: Links the additional inner-shell electrons to increased shielding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that inner-shell electrons shield outer electrons, or stating that shielding increases.

modelAnswer: Down a group, each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
These inner-shell electrons shield the outer electrons from nuclear attraction, so the shielding effect increases.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy greater than the second ionization energy?

rubric.why: Removing the first electron leaves a positively charged ion.
rubric.description: Identifies the ion formed after the first electron is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the atom becomes a positive ion.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons are more strongly attracted to the nucleus, so removing another electron requires more energy.
rubric.description: Explains why removal of the second electron requires greater energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stronger nuclear attraction with the greater energy required.

modelAnswer: After the first ionization, the atom becomes a positively charged ion.
The remaining electrons experience stronger attraction to the nucleus, so more energy is needed to remove the second electron.

items.followUp: Why are gases easily compressed compared with solids?

rubric.why: Gas particles are separated by large spaces.
rubric.description: States that gas particles are far apart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to the large spaces between gas particles.

rubric.why: Large spaces mean that a given volume contains little matter, giving gases low density.
rubric.description: Connects the particle spacing with low mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the large spaces result in little matter, or low mass, per unit volume.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are very far apart, with large spaces between them.
Therefore, a given volume contains little matter and gases have low density.

items.followUp: How can you distinguish between pure water and a salt solution by evaporation?

accept: pure liquid evaporates without leaving residue
rubric.why: A pure liquid evaporates without leaving dissolved material behind.
rubric.description: States what happens to a pure liquid on evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that the pure liquid leaves no residue.

rubric.why: When the solvent evaporates, the dissolved solute remains as residue.
rubric.description: States what happens to a solution on evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that a solution leaves dissolved solute or residue behind.

modelAnswer: Evaporate a sample of the liquid to dryness.
A pure liquid leaves no residue, whereas a solution leaves its dissolved solute as a residue.
